exceptions.reason: Existing #152/#124/#125 deterministic basic-Latin question-mark fallback and its different advances for unsupported RTL scalars. Physical line anchoring and bidi order remain as specified. Under the user-approved spec §8.5 per-glyph device-phase rule, these axis-aligned glyphs retain the whole-device-Y baseline and use quarter-device-pixel X origins; this replaces the former whole-line-only baseline placement. The separate #168 SVG harness direction/paragraph limitation and its measured SVG pin remain unchanged. The direct-PNG limits are remeasured only for the approved per-glyph placement, with unchanged SVG output and verified outline/run partitions.

purpose: Lay out right-to-left and direction-mixed text at every textAlign as spec 8.3 requires after #166: one Hebrew line at textAlign left, center and right, a right-to-left element (Hebrew first line) whose second line starts with Latin and reads `world 123 <Arabic> Hello` in visual order at the element's level, and a left-to-right element (Latin first line) whose second line starts with Hebrew and reads `123 <Hebrew> world`, all in Excalifont at 20 px and 300 wide so the anchored side of every line is judged. No bundled face maps a Hebrew or Arabic scalar, so every right-to-left run is spec 8.3's deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans, one font.missing-glyph per scalar per occurrence in logical order, while the official export draws the pinned container's FreeSans for Hebrew and FreeSerif for Arabic (#124). The direct PNG judges the alignment against the official canvas, which anchors each line physically. The SVG raster dimension cannot: the official exporter writes every right-to-left element with text-anchor end and direction rtl, which usvg resolves without regard to direction, so the left-aligned right-to-left elements land off the canvas under the harness rasterizer (#168), and the case's SVG raster measurement is held as a rasterizer limitation pin; the right-aligned right-to-left element's official SVG overflows in Chromium, the reference authority divergence spec 8.3 records, which that rasterizer does not see.
